explanations: toCents multiplies a binary float by 100 and truncates. Many decimal amounts are not exactly representable: parseFloat("19.99") * 100 is 1998.9999999999998 and parseFloat("0.29") * 100 is 28.999999999999996, so Math.trunc yields 1998 and 28. Billed totals are silently understated by a cent on many lines, which skews reconciliation and dispute amounts. Parse the integer and fractional parts as strings, or at least use Math.round.

Lines are summed per tracking number in billedPerShipment (1,200), then compared once against the quote: 1,200 - 1,000 = 200 > 50, giving one overcharge of 200. Lines are not compared individually, and the shipment is known so no unknown_shipment.

totalBilledCents is incremented before the currency check, so every line counts. The expected total is accumulated only in the second loop over billedPerShipment, which contains a tracking number only if at least one line had matching currency. Mismatched lines are never added to disputableCents.

AMOUNT_RE allows a leading minus, so the credit parses as -300. Lines are summed per tracking number to 2,000, which equals the quote, so delta is 0 and nothing is reported. There is no credit discrepancy kind, and per-line comparison does not happen.
